headline: Meta hit with $25 billion penalty in New Mexico
caption:
A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for 43 million deception violations, 5 times the $5 billion the FTC fined Facebook in 2019. State law allows $5,000 a violation, about $215 billion, and Judge Francis Mathew cut the total; Meta says it does not sell user data and will appeal, and the proceeds go to New Mexico's schools.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Brent Hits $110.63 After Houthi Drone Strike
caption:
Brent crude hit $110.63 after a Houthi drone strike on Saudi Arabia's Shaybah oil field, where debris from intercepted drones killed 2 workers, a Filipino and a Nepali. The Energy Ministry says Shaybah's output was unaffected.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 630 Drones Head for Moscow in Ukraine’s Largest Attack
caption:
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 630 drones headed for the Moscow region overnight, the largest drone attack on the capital this year, with 163 shot down as they approached the city. Two people were injured in the Voronovo district, Sobyanin said.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: First known human death from Shamonda virus recorded in France
caption:
A Lyon-area man in his 60s has died infected with Shamonda virus, previously known only in animals, in what would be the first known human case, French authorities say. Investigators suspect a midge bite infected the immunocompromised patient, and officials see no risk to the general population.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Guterres: West Bank settler violence is out of control
caption:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres said Israeli settlers attack Palestinians in the West Bank daily, aiming to drive communities off their land. He also said settlers target journalists and diplomats, and that Gaza aid remains severely restricted ahead of winter.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 16 dead after magnitude 7.0 quake hits Tibet
caption:
A 7.0 earthquake in China's Tibet region, 390km from Lhasa, killed 16 people, injured 32 and brought down 300 houses, authorities say. Power and telecoms are down in the county seat of Baqen, Xinhua said, and the US Geological Survey put the quake's depth at 10km.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Threatens Data Centres and Undersea Cables in 7 Gulf States
caption:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said cables, data centres and AI sites in 7 Gulf states would be hit if US-Israeli strikes resume. US officials say Trump has made no final decision, with the earliest window after the 3 November midterms.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Ebola Has Killed 4,600 and Reached Nigeria
caption:
Ebola has killed more than 4,600 people and reached Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, where no proven vaccine exists for the Bundibugyo strain. WHO says the source of the Nigerian patient's infection remains unknown, and Africa's disease agency had left Nigeria off its initial list of 15 at-risk countries.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Moderna-Merck vaccine cuts melanoma relapse or death by 42%
caption:
Moderna and Merck's personalized melanoma vaccine cut the risk of relapse or death by 42% in a Phase 3 trial of more than 1,100 patients, below the 49% seen in the earlier Phase 2b study, and Moderna shares, up 500% this year, fell. Citi questioned whether the benefit justifies making each dose from the patient's own tumour, given with Keytruda.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Gunman kills one, wounds four including girl, 12, in Trappes
caption:
A gunman firing from a car at a playground, a fuel station and a medical centre in Trappes, France, killed 1 person and wounded 4, including a 12-year-old girl. French antiterrorism prosecutors are investigating a racial or religious motive, and the town's mayor called the shooting a terrorist attack.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Two supertankers carrying 4.5 million barrels hit mines in Hormuz
caption:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say 2 supertankers carrying 4.5 million barrels hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, disabling both engine rooms, a claim not independently verified. US Central Command says forces have cleared the shipping lanes and 95% of vessels get through.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Rubio Invites Cubans to Partner With US Intelligence
caption:
Rubio invited Cubans into a "discrete partnership" with US intelligence in a CIA Spanish-language video that tells informants to visit a US facility or use a secure connection and burner email. Cuba's Deputy Foreign Minister Carlos Fernandez de Cossio said it shows "a great deal of desperation or misery within the agency."

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Gunmen kill 8 and wound 40 at funeral in Jordan
caption:
Gunmen killed 8 and wounded 40 at a funeral outside a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, firing for minutes on 150 to 200 mourners, a witness said. The attackers remain at large and no group has claimed responsibility.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Jio’s record share offer fills in 100 minutes
caption:
Jio's record share offer drew bids of Rs 7.4 lakh crore against a Rs 30,188 crore issue, 22.19 times subscribed, the company says. The offer filled in 100 minutes, and the shares list on India's two main exchanges on 28 October.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 410,000 march across France as Paris protest turns to tear gas
caption:
Police in France arrested 135 people and fired tear gas and water cannon in Paris on Saturday as 410,000 marched nationwide against Marine Le Pen's National Rally and President Emmanuel Macron, the government says. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said police seized lead pellets, fireworks and a katana.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Fire destroys Hitler’s Eagle’s Nest; 33-year-old detained
caption:
Fire destroys the Eagle's Nest in Berchtesgaden, the Nazi-era guest house that draws 350,000 visitors a year, and police have detained a 33-year-old. Prosecutor Rainer Vietze says arson looks likely, and the man is provisionally held in psychiatric care.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: New York Archdiocese to pay $800 million to 1,300 abuse survivors
caption:
The New York archdiocese will pay $800 million to 1,300 clergy abuse survivors, the second-largest US settlement of its kind after Los Angeles's $880 million in 2024. Each survivor is expected to receive at least $250,000, and the deal ends years of litigation without a trial.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Obama Blames Iran War for Rising Diesel Prices
caption:
Obama, campaigning in Cleveland, blamed the Iran war for rising diesel prices ahead of 3 November Senate and governor races in Ohio and Michigan. Polymarket traders give Democrats a 67% chance of winning the Senate, up 2 points in a week.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Could Strike Iran as Soon as Sunday
caption:
President Trump says the US may strike Iran as soon as Sunday, with a US media report saying a renewed campaign could hit Iranian energy facilities, infrastructure and nuclear sites. Central Command has reportedly prepared strike options for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and only Trump can order them.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months in exile
caption:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has re-entered Venezuela after 10 months abroad, by an undisclosed route, as talks between the interim government and a rival opposition faction exclude her movement. President Donald Trump said he knew nothing of her return, and her adviser David Smolansky says she will press for an election date.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Serbia’s Vucic concedes defeat to student-led list
caption:
Serbia's Vucic said his Progressive Party lost to the Students' List, a movement born of student protests, Russian state news agency TASS reported. He predicted the new government will sanction Russia by March or April, though the Students' List says it rejects such sanctions.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Saudi Arabia intercepts 10 ballistic missiles as Houthis claim pipeline strike
caption:
Saudi Arabia's air defences intercepted 10 ballistic missiles on Sunday, and the Houthis claim they hit the East-West pipeline, Riyadh's crude export route that avoids Hormuz. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed any hit; Civil Defense said debris from two missiles injured 2 people in Khamis Mushait.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Israel’s army chief warned US against striking Iran
caption:
Israel's army chief, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, reportedly demanded signed legal authorisation before carrying out a directive that risked a flare-up with Iran, as Netanyahu reportedly pressed the US for joint strikes before Tuesday's election. Defence Minister Katz says Israel had no intention of attacking Iran before the vote.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Anthropic loses $80.7bn on $16.3bn revenue in IPO filing
caption:
Anthropic lost $80.7 billion on $16.3 billion of revenue over six months, according to its filing for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. Most of the loss reflects a rise in the fair value of convertible bonds, and the filing sets no price range for the November target.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Israel votes Tuesday with Eisenkot 8 to 10 points ahead
caption:
Israel votes Tuesday with polls putting Eisenkot 8 to 10 points ahead of Netanyahu, but Netanyahu could lose and still remain caretaker prime minister while seeking another vote. Polls give Eisenkot enough seats only with Arab party backing, which his partner Avigdor Liberman rules out.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Comey Indicted a Third Time Over 2016 Leak Case
caption:
Prosecutors have charged former FBI Director James Comey a third time under President Donald Trump's administration, reviving a closed 2016 leak case with a criminal information that charges him with transmitting national defense information without an indictment. The filing was made this month and unsealed Monday; Comey's lawyers say it came too late, and a judge will decide whether to dismiss it.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Saudi Defence Minister Meets Iran’s President in Tehran
caption:
Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran on Monday, while Houthi missiles hit Saudi airports and oil sites. A Pakistani security official said Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia discussed a regional non-aggression network, and no participant announced any agreement on Hormuz, the US blockade or the Houthi attacks.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Audi announces $4 billion Georgia plant on Trump’s stage
caption:
Audi announced a $4 billion plant in Georgia to build 200,000 SUVs a year at a Trump event, and works council head Daniela Cavallo and IG Metall's Christiane Benner say CEO Gernot Döllner breached Audi's election-neutrality rules. Tariffs of 15% cost Audi an estimated €1.2bn last year, and it has no US factory.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran’s Unseen Supreme Leader Backs War Conditions
caption:
Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei, unseen in public since March, has backed Tehran's condition that the US end its blockade before any talks, while Washington demands Iran drop its nuclear ambitions, state media reported. Polymarket traders give a US-Iran Hormuz agreement by 2 November a 6% chance, down 8 points in a week.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Britain charges two men over Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford bomber base
caption:
Britain has charged two men, one with assisting Iranian intelligence, after vans were driven to RAF Fairford, where about a dozen B-1 bombers had been evacuated in October. Prosecutors say Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, 24, arranged for five men to drive vans to the base for a handler called Ali; Iran denies involvement.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Flávio Bolsonaro slips out of Brazil, bypassing border posts
caption:
Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil through no regular border post, a police official said, after police cancelled Bolsonaro's passports Tuesday under a Supreme Court order in a money-laundering probe. A US administration official said Washington will issue visas to Bolsonaro and family.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: North Korea aims three howitzers south from Kaepung
caption:
North Korea deployed 3 self-propelled 122-millimeter howitzers aimed at South Korea from Kaepung on Monday, after September landmine blasts injured 3 South Korean soldiers that Seoul blames on Pyongyang. Pyongyang denies causing the blasts, and both Koreas have written to the UN Security Council president.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: At least 10 dead as two high-speed trains collide in Spain
caption:
At least 10 people died when one high-speed train ran into the back of a stopped train near Toledo, Spain, knocking two cars off the track, regional officials said. It is Spain's second deadly high-speed crash this year, after 45 deaths in January.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Neither Israeli bloc reaches 61 seats without Arab parties
caption:
Neither Netanyahu's bloc, with about 54 seats, nor Eisenkot's, with 49, reaches 61 in Israel's 120-seat Knesset without Ra'am and the Joint List, which won 17 seats, and neither bloc has agreed to partner with them. Counting is unfinished.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Markets now fully price a December Fed rate hike
caption:
The Federal Reserve held rates steady while markets now fully price a December hike, with inflation at 3% or higher against a 2% target and oil up about 20% since September to around $114 a barrel. The Fed's statement gave no clear signal on a December move, saying more information will guide its stance.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump demands Peltola be prosecuted over a second Sullivan on Alaska ballot
caption:
Trump wants Mary Peltola prosecuted after text messages showed her Alaska campaign discussed recruiting a namesake of Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan for the ranked-choice ballot. Peltola's campaign and the second Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher, deny any coordination, and Alaskans vote 3 November.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Warns Gulf States of Iran Strikes After 3 November
caption:
Iran's security officials have drawn up plans to attack Gulf undersea cables if US strikes resume, as the US moves a carrier group, a Marine unit and a Patriot system to join about 20 warships in the region next month. A senior Iranian official called Qatar's seven-day plan unacceptable and not an offer, and Tehran owes Qatar a response by the end of the week.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russian drone kills at least 13 on Dnipro railway platform
caption:
A Russian drone strike on a railway platform in Dnipro killed at least 13 people, Ukrainian officials say. Russia's Defence Ministry says Ukraine launched a record 1,214 drones at 20 regions overnight, and Moscow's mayor said 613 targeted the capital region.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Lagarde to leave the ECB on 7 February 2027
caption:
Christine Lagarde will leave the European Central Bank on 7 February 2027, and EU leaders plan to name her successor before a French election that polls say Marine Le Pen is favoured to win. Council President Antonio Costa opened the appointment process Thursday, with Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernández de Cos seen as frontrunners.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: DoorDash buys Instacart in $17 billion deal
caption:
DoorDash plans to buy Instacart in a $17 billion deal that would put gig workers at both apps under one company, pending approval from federal regulators. Gridwise data show Instacart workers average about $13 an hour and DoorDash workers about $11, and CEO Tony Xu promised "greater earning opportunities" without committing to higher pay.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Italian Chinook crashes in Bosnia, killing four and injuring 11
caption:
An Italian Chinook helicopter crashed in Bosnia near Brčko, killing 4 and injuring 11, Italy's defence ministry said. The dead were two soldiers and two Red Cross volunteers, and the European Union force there is investigating.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers Steal $5.9 Billion From Binance, Chainalysis Confirms
caption:
Chainalysis has confirmed at least $5.9 billion stolen from Binance, which says it will cover all losses and has suspended deposits and withdrawals. Tether and Circle froze more than $2.3 billion in stablecoins, but bitcoin has no issuer to freeze it.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Pentagon asks 3 Baltic states to soften Russia warnings
caption:
Pentagon officials have asked Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to soften their public warnings about Russia, four sources say, while the US reviews its troop levels in Europe. Policy chief Elbridge Colby delivered the message privately, the sources said, and the review could end in a sharp drawdown.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Dockworkers at 110 ports in 22 countries stop work over Gaza
caption:
Dockworkers at 110 ports in 22 countries stopped work over arms shipments to Israel, with campaign group No Harbour for Genocide tracking 315 Elbit Systems shipments through 56 ports since August 2025. Only 5 countries called 24-hour strikes, while Morocco and Cyprus stop for up to 2 hours.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Brent hits $117.56, up 15% in October
caption:
Brent crude rose to $117.56 a barrel, up about 15% in October and a fourth straight monthly gain, after Iran's Revolutionary Guard said a tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday. West Texas Intermediate is up about 12% for the month, and Qatar's mediators have returned to Tehran.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer who admitted on camera to hitting fleeing m
caption:
Harris County prosecutors have indicted immigration officer Mario Alberto Morales for aggravated assault, a rare charge against a federal immigration officer, after surveillance footage contradicted the agency's account that Miguel Parra-Hernandez, 48, ran in front of a vehicle. District Attorney Sean Teare's office is still investigating the July 7 fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, blamed on officer Gregory Feathers.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Tennessee fails to execute Christa Pike with two lethal doses
caption:
Two lethal injections on September 30 failed to kill Tennessee death-row inmate Christa Pike, convicted of the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer, her lawyers say, because the drug pooled in her arms instead of entering her bloodstream. Governor Bill Lee suspects her sentence will stand unless courts decide otherwise, and an independent review is pending.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russia vetoes US draft on Western Sahara mission
caption:
Russia vetoed a US Security Council draft backed by 11 members that would renew the Western Sahara mission, with the mandate set to expire Saturday. The US text dropped "referendum" from the mission's name and made Morocco's autonomy plan the sole basis for talks, and Morocco's royal palace said UN personnel and equipment should leave the territory.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Over 30 ships attacked near Hormuz in October, a record
caption:
More than 30 attacks hit ships near the Strait of Hormuz in October, a record and more than double September's total, UK Maritime Trade Operations data show. US Central Command says over 95% of ships transit safely, while Brent crude stood at $117.60 on 30 October.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 43 million Americans have already voted, 10 million more than 2022
caption:
43 million Americans have voted early before Tuesday's US midterms, 10 million more than in 2022, with Democrats needing a net 4 seats to take a Senate Republicans hold 53-47. Sabato's Crystal Ball analyst Kyle Kondik says the House is almost certain to flip and the Senate far less settled.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US Warns of Mass-Casualty Attack in Moscow on Saturday
caption:
The US warned of a mass-casualty attack at Moscow's Tsaritsyno on Saturday, and Russia's Federal Security Service said the US tipped it off. Washington gave a similar warning weeks before the 2024 Crocus City Hall attack that killed over 100. Neither government has named a suspect or said whether anyone is in custody.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Rubio Sees Growing Interest in a Black Sea Ceasefire
caption:
US Secretary of State Rubio says interest is growing in a Black Sea ceasefire, as the US reviews Turkish and Indian proposals to halt attacks on grain ships and, in some cases, energy cargoes. Ukraine and Russia, both major wheat exporters, are now attacking each other's ships, and Canada's foreign minister said Russia has not shown it is willing to move ahead.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: FBI Blames North Korea for $6.3 Billion Binance Theft
caption:
The FBI says North Korea's TraderTraitor group stole $6.3 billion from Binance and is now moving the funds into Ethereum. Bitcoin fell about 5% after the theft, and the FBI has asked exchanges to block transactions linked to the suspect wallets.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Qatari LNG carrier struck near Hormuz amid Iran-US talks
caption:
Qatar Gas Transport Company said unidentified objects struck its LNG carrier Al Mayeda on Friday evening, causing no injuries, and the vessel remains operational. People with direct knowledge say Pakistan had negotiated Iranian safe passage for the ship beforehand, and the company's statement names no attacker.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Adviser Warns Retaliation Will Reach Beyond West Asia
caption:
Iran will retaliate beyond West Asia, state news agency Mehr reported, citing Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Ayatollah Khamenei, and Russia's TASS carried the same post. Mehr said Khamenei told commanders on Saturday to prepare a response with no geographic limits, while neither report names a weapon, a range or a target.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Ukraine claims record 54,400 Russian casualties in October
caption:
Ukraine's General Staff says Russia lost 54,400 soldiers killed, wounded or missing in October, a monthly record, in a count Kyiv itself compiled. President Zelensky said Ukraine retook 37 square miles while Russia reportedly took 33, and that only a Russian ceasefire would stop the losses.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Netanyahu Urges Trump to Strike Iran After Midterms
caption:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing President Donald Trump to strike Iran after the US midterm elections, sources say, as the White House weighs renewed combat while Qatari-mediated talks continue. Trump said the US could hit the suspected nuclear site at Pickaxe Mountain "in 10 minutes," while Iran's foreign minister says no agreement exists yet.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Rioters Injure Over 100 Police in Frankfurt
caption:
Rioters injured more than 100 of 1,300 police deployed at a Frankfurt youth protest over education and living costs, with 54 arrested, 17 stores damaged and 5 looted, Hesse's interior minister said. Germany's ministers promise severe penalties, while Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed immigrant-community troublemakers without evidence, though most of those arrested were German nationals.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Cyberattacks heat freezers to 50°C in dozens of European supermarkets
caption:
Freezers in dozens of European supermarkets reached 50°C overnight in an apparent cyberattack, and a Belgian butcher says it ruined €15,000 of meat. Sabcobel's chief executive says attackers switched evaporators to defrost mode, while Carrefour Belgium says only 15 of its 700 stores were affected.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Cuts Hormuz Reopening Offer From 7 Days to 2
caption:
Iran has cut its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz from 7 days to 2, conditional on the US ending its blockade of Iranian ports, unfreezing assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the war on all fronts. US and Israeli military officials are drafting plans for renewed strikes after the 3 November midterms.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Generic HIV prevention shot to cost $40 a year, not $28,218
caption:
Generic lenacapavir, the twice-yearly HIV prevention shot, is expected to cost $40 a year instead of $28,218 after the US FDA tentatively approved India's Dr. Reddy's Laboratories version. It opens supply to 120 low- and middle-income countries, though generics from other licensed makers still await approval and some countries require national sign-off first.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Midterms become a vote on Trump’s Iran war
caption:
Diesel hit a record $6.52 a gallon in September as the Iran war pushed up fuel prices, putting cost of living at the center of midterm races that will decide control of the Senate. Democrats need a net gain of 4 seats, with contests in Michigan, Texas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine, Alaska and North Carolina.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: North Korea denies stealing $6.3bn from Binance
caption:
Kim Yo-jong denied that North Korea stole $6.3bn from Binance, the largest crypto theft on record, which the FBI attributes to Pyongyang's TraderTraitor group. President Trump told reporters in Florida, "We don't know if it's North Korea," and US investigators have yet to publish their forensics.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers set fridges to 50C across seven European countries
caption:
Suspected hackers set commercial fridges to 50C across 7 European countries, and UK meat suppliers lost stock, though a National Cyber Security Centre official calls the impact minimal. Researchers found more than 800 refrigeration and building-control interfaces exposed to the public internet, and no group has claimed responsibility.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump says $4 billion in Israel military aid ends at year-end
caption:
Trump says $4 billion in US aid to Israel will stop at year-end, though Congress appropriates the money and a 10-year memorandum signed in 2016 runs through 2028. Netanyahu's office has not responded, and a Chicago Council poll found 68% of Republicans favour continuing aid.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Demands Recognition of Hormuz Sovereignty in Five Conditions
caption:
Iran demands recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, plus sanctions relief, war reparations and a guarantee against future attack, in terms that exceed what mediators seek, Tasnim reported. Armed forces chief Ali Abdollahi's plan goes beyond the proposed swap of an end to Hormuz attacks for a lifted US blockade.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Greenland’s parliament approves US security deal 16-0
caption:
Greenland's parliament passed a US security deal 16-0 with 7 abstentions, expanding US operations at Pituffik Space Base and keeping them in place even if Greenland becomes independent. The deal takes effect only after Denmark ratifies it, with Danish lawmakers set to debate it later this month.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Democrats flip 6 Senate seats and win the House
caption:
Democrats flipped 6 Senate seats and won the House, gaining subpoena power over the Trump administration for the final two years of his term. President Donald Trump said of the losses, "I think a part of it was Iran," as AP polling found 4 in 10 voters ranked the economy first, citing petrol prices that rose after the Iran war began.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Abdul El-Sayed Becomes America’s First Muslim Senator
caption:
Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate race to become the first Muslim in the US Senate, while Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man elected to the chamber. Keisha Lance Bottoms and Deb Haaland also won governorships in Georgia and New Mexico, as the first Black woman and first Native American woman to lead those states, and Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first Black House speaker when Democrats take control in January.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hackers tried to overheat French blood bank plasma storage
caption:
Attackers targeted the refrigeration control systems at 3 French blood-storage sites in an attempt to push plasma temperatures past boiling, but the French Blood Establishment says no products were lost and distribution never stopped. Monitoring alarms flagged the anomalies, and the cybersecurity agency and Health Ministry are investigating without naming a suspect.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Israel displaces nearly 5,000 Palestinians in Hebron in 11 days
caption:
Israel's army displaced nearly 5,000 Palestinians from Hebron in 11 days, sealing the city's entrances and disrupting schooling for 80,000 students. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the army is prepared for an extensive operation across the West Bank.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Hubert Aiwanger, 55, found dead in Berlin hotel room
caption:
Hubert Aiwanger, 55, leader of the Free Voters and deputy to Bavarian Minister-President Markus Soeder, was found dead in a Berlin hotel room. Police sources say the cause appears health-related with no sign of foul play, and prosecutors have opened an inquest.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Joshua Wong’s release pushed back nine years, to 2036
caption:
Hong Kong court extends Joshua Wong's jail term by nearly a decade, moving his release from January 2027 to November 2036 after a conviction for lobbying foreign governments for sanctions. Judge William Tam set 13 years as the starting point, then cut 3 for Wong's September guilty plea.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Another tanker hits a mine east of Hormuz
caption:
Another tanker hit a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy says, in a waterway that normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption and that Iran calls closed to uncoordinated ships. The navy said the vessel had switched off its tracking systems.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Paraguay’s president resigns after bank serving 60% of adults collapses
caption:
Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigned Thursday, hours after regulators seized Ueno Bank, which counted 60% of the country's adults as customers. Prosecutors have charged 27 Ueno officials, and insured deposits of up to $38,000 per person must be paid within 15 days.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Newsom commutes all 548 California death sentences
caption:
Gov. Gavin Newsom commuted all 548 death sentences in California, home to the Western Hemisphere's largest death row, to life in prison on Thursday. Victims' advocates say they will challenge the commutations in court.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Saudi Arabia’s $5 billion LIV Golf bet ends in liquidation
caption:
Saudi Arabia's $5 billion LIV Golf venture is being liquidated after a $300 million BC Partners rescue collapsed when top players, including Dustin Johnson and Bryson DeChambeau, declined to sign. Seven executives received $15.6 million before the 8 September bankruptcy filing, including CEO Scott O'Neil's $6.375 million.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Judge Freezes Trump’s Arch Hours After Approval
caption:
A US judge has frozen construction of Trump's 250-foot arch in Washington for 14 days, hours after the planning commission approved it 8-4. The National Park Service says the arch could harm as many as 42 historic sites.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: South Korea halts trading as Kospi plunges 8%
caption:
South Korea halted trading Friday after the Kospi fell 8%, as the AI-driven selloff spread across Asia and Taiwan's benchmark lost 12.2% this week. Cleanview data show 40% of pending US data-centre capacity sits in states whose new Democratic governors promised pauses.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: $1.26 billion in crypto bets wiped out as Bitcoin falls below $75,000
caption:
Bitcoin fell below $75,000 for the first time since 15 September as the Nasdaq dropped 5.5%, and CoinGlass says $1.26 billion in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $430.2 million Thursday, SoSoValue data show.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Stephen Miller to run the White House from Monday
caption:
President Trump named Stephen Miller, the architect of his deportation policy, White House chief of staff to replace Susie Wiles, effective Monday, after the midterm defeat. Miller previously set US immigration agents a target of 3,000 arrests a day, and Democrats, who take both chambers in January, are expected to investigate him.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Three Ships Sunk in a Week in the Strait of Hormuz
caption:
Three ships sank in the Strait of Hormuz in 7 days, and UK Maritime Trade Operations counted 11 attacks through 4 November, 8 in the strait and 3 in the Arabian Gulf. A projectile strike on a dhow on 2 November killed 1 crew member.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US offers up to $20 million for tips on Iran’s nuclear program
caption:
The US State Department is offering up to $20 million and relocation to informants on Iran's nuclear program, saying Iran's non-compliance cost the UN nuclear watchdog track of its centrifuge production and inventory. Senior US officials point to the moonless night of 9 November as Trump weighs renewed strikes.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US projectiles hit Iran’s Qeshm island again
caption:
Two US projectiles struck Iran's Qeshm island Friday night, as UK maritime monitors log at least 11 ships attacked near Hormuz in a week, 3 of them sunk. Iran's navy said a tanker with its transponder off hit a mine and caught fire in the eastern strait, while Washington says the mines were cleared.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Gunman kills six in Kraków’s Main Square
caption:
A gunman who drove into Kraków's Main Square and fired at random from his car killed 6 people, police said. Officers gave conflicting accounts on whether he had accomplices, and no motive has been given.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: US aircraft fires on cargo ship leaving Iran
caption:
US Central Command says its blockade of Iran now extends to the country's land borders and the Caspian Sea, after a US aircraft fired on a cargo ship leaving Iran. A new 20-person task force in Tampa will coordinate efforts on weapons, dual-use goods and revenue.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Two tankers burn after hitting mines in Hormuz
caption:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say 2 tankers are burning after hitting mines in and east of the Strait of Hormuz, and warn any ship leaving Iran's authorised route will strike a mine. The Guards named neither ship, and no outside party has confirmed the mines.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Europe’s largest nuclear plant runs on diesel generators
caption:
Europe's largest nuclear plant, Zaporizhzhia, is running on diesel generators after losing its last working 330 kV power line, its 16th complete blackout of 2026, Energoatom said. Energoatom says Russia is deliberately disabling the lines, while the plant's own report names no cause, and warns fuel cooling is at risk if the generators fail or run out of fuel.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Russian strikes cut power to 850,000 people
caption:
Russian strikes cut power to about 850,000 people in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions, energy provider DTEK said, as repeated attacks slow repairs ahead of winter. Russia's defence ministry said it will keep striking energy sites it says aid Ukraine's army.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Egypt train collision kills 7, injures 112
caption:
Egypt's Health Ministry says 7 people died and 112 were injured when a Giza-to-Fayoum train rammed the rear of a Cairo-to-Aswan service in al-Ayyat, derailing carriages onto a road. Al-Ayyat is where more than 370 people died in Egypt's worst rail disaster, a 2002 train fire.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump holds 38 Iranian bridges at risk as talks open
caption:
Trump holds 38 Iranian bridges at risk, tying restraint to a nuclear deal and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, as an Iraqi delegation spent 8 hours in Tehran delivering a US message, unnamed sources said. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Washington must choose between a deal and war.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump vows comeback after midterm loss as Miller becomes chief of staff
caption:
Democrats have won both chambers of Congress, with the Senate count at 54 to 44, gaining power to summon officials, demand documents and hold hearings. Incoming oversight chair Robert Garcia plans to question Elon Musk and Stephen Miller, the new White House chief of staff, in January.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 20 Migrants Dead Off Crete, 12 Bodies Pulled From One Boat
caption:
Greece's coast guard says 20 migrants have died trying to reach Crete in recent days, including 12 bodies recovered from one boat off Kali Limenes. Frontex rescued 87 more people from two boats about 56 kilometres south of the port.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Viktor Orbán’s brother detained in Hungary raids
caption:
Police in Hungary have reportedly detained Áron Orbán, brother of Viktor Orbán, in raids tied to a probe into a network that allegedly sold work visas to foreigners. Viktor Orbán calls the case political, saying "I am the target, my younger brother is just a tool."

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 16 workers killed in Turkish steel plant explosion
caption:
16 workers were killed and 13 injured at the Habaş steel plant in Aliağa, Turkey, after a ceiling crane collapsed into an electric arc furnace and damaged a natural gas line, the governor said. President Erdoğan said 4 prosecutors have been assigned, and the mayor says the final toll awaits cleared debris.
Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline set ablaze in unclaimed attack
caption:
An unclaimed attack set fire to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the kingdom's main crude export route since the US-Israeli war closed the Strait of Hormuz. The energy ministry said operations were unaffected and no one was hurt.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Trump Holds Iran Strikes After Gulf Allies Ask
caption:
President Trump is holding off on new strikes on Iran after Gulf neighbours asked him to, while Israel's Netanyahu presses him daily to resume, a briefed person said. Iran offers free Hormuz shipping if the US lifts its port blockade, frees frozen assets and restarts final-deal talks.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran hacked freezers in 700 French supermarkets, prosecutors say
caption:
France says Iran's Revolutionary Guards heated freezers in 700 French supermarkets, which prosecutors call the first large-scale cyber sabotage on French soil. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot summoned Iran's ambassador and is seeking EU sanctions, which need all 27 member states to agree.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: 1,000 TikTok abuse videos drew 48 million views
caption:
Spain's youth ministry is weighing a TikTok suspension and has asked prosecutors to act, after fact-checkers Maldita.es reported 1,000 abuse videos drew 48 million views. Maldita.es says TikTok's algorithm recommended 19 livestreams by minors in 3 days.

Full story in the app — link in bio.

headline: Iran Sets Seven Conditions for Talks, Denies Any US Contact
caption:
Iran says the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until the US meets 7 conditions, and that Washington has given no clear response, security official Mohsen Rezaei told Al-Mayadeen. President Trump rejected Iran's truce plan after meeting mediator Qatar on Monday, while playing down a return to war.

Full story in the app — link in bio.
